question: What minimal dense embedding scale and which specific dense modes (citation heritage, section cross-lingual, linear hybrid complement) are necessary and sufficient for the product's non-jurist-preference views?
hypothesis: Dense embeddings (multilingual-e5 center_projected) are COMPLEMENTARY to TF-IDF citation hybrids (PRIMARY) for the product's multi-view map. They excel at: (1) Citation Heritage Recovery (AUC 0.79-0.85 > TF-IDF 0.71-0.74), minimal scale ~130k; (2) Section Cross-lingual Alignment (Sachverhalt > Dispositiv > Erwaegungen), full corpus BLOCKED; (3) Linear Hybrid Complement (PASS adversarial at 19yr+ w=0.3-0.4, adds cross-lingual benefit but JP < TF-IDF baseline).
baseline: TF-IDF citation hybrids (cited_decisions_tfidf_outcome_hybrid_0.5) at 174k: JP=0.73-0.78, LangDom=0.48, PASS both adversarial gates.
success_rule: Characterize minimal sufficient scale and specific dense modes for each complementary view with evidence from max available scale (144k/22yr). No claim-bearing measurement — this is a descriptive characterization of ACCEPTED evidence.

citation_heritage_view.scale_dependency: Capability emerges when sufficient cross-year citation pairs exist (years 2019+). 21yr: raw AUC 0.8455, cp64 AUC 0.8182 (100 pairs). 22yr: raw AUC 0.7946, cp64 AUC 0.7922 (344 pairs).

section_crosslingual_view.current_evidence_scale: 1K sample (Sachverhalt n=359, Dispositiv n=538, Erwaegungen n=510)

product_integration.status: SAMPLE ONLY — BLOCKED pending section extraction at 174k

linear_hybrid_complement.necessary: For cross-lingual benefit in hybrid mode
linear_hybrid_complement.minimal_scale: 122k decisions (19-year, 2000-2018) — first scale PASS both adversarial gates
linear_hybrid_complement.note: Does NOT beat TF-IDF on jurist preference — marked exploratory mode
linear_hybrid_complement.acceptance_criteria: PASS both adversarial gates AND cross_lang_same_branch > TF-IDF baseline

two_mode_tradeoff.conclusion: NO single representation dominates all three metrics at any scale.

data_blockers.bge_bger_id_mapping: Canonical corpus uses bge_ IDs, evaluation uses bger_ IDs — no mapping exists

next_recommendation: COMPLEMENTARY ROLE CHARACTERIZED at max available scale (144k/22yr). Dense embeddings are NECESSARY and SUFFICIENT for two non-jurist-preference views: (1) Citation Heritage — center_projected_64dim AUC 0.79-0.85 > TF-IDF 0.71-0.74, minimal scale ~130k (21yr); (2) Section Cross-lingual — Sachverhalt > Dispositiv > Erwaegungen hierarchy, center_projected_64dim improves all sections 16-38%, full corpus BLOCKED pending section extraction; (3) Linear Hybrid Complement — PASS adversarial at 19yr+ with w=0.3-0.4, adds cross-lingual benefit but BELOW TF-IDF baseline on JP. TF-IDF citation hybrids = PRIMARY (JP 0.78); Dense = COMPLEMENTARY. Data blockers: bge_/bger_ ID mapping + parquet 2022-2026 + section extraction. Corpus lane resumption required for 174k completion.
